minutes.headline: Finance Committee put most April town meeting articles on a consent calendar but pulled Article 27 for explanation.
minutes.summary: The committee reviewed which warrant articles go on the consent calendar for the spring town meeting, voted to include a list but exclude Article 27 (adding positions to the pay grid). They discussed position and salary information, school contract negotiations and the school salary reserve, and agreed to revisit it in June. They also discussed a capital planning committee recommendation to raise the capital threshold, deferring a vote to a future agenda, and heard committee and town manager reports.

what_happened.line: The committee voted by roll call, all aye, to put a list of town meeting articles on the consent calendar, leaving out Article 27, which adds positions to the pay grid.
The consent calendar may be revisited before town meeting, since more articles could be passed over.
Members discussed the schools' salary reserve for next year and several unsettled school contracts, and agreed to take up position and salary information again in June.
A capital planning committee recommendation to raise the capital project threshold was discussed, but no vote was taken; language will be sought on a future agenda.

why_it_matters: Articles on the consent calendar pass together without separate discussion at town meeting, so Article 27, which adds positions to the pay grid, is the one that will get its own explanation and vote.
The schools' salary reserve covers next year only while several contracts are unsettled, so how raises are absorbed is an open question that bears on future tax bills.
Raising the capital threshold would change which purchases are treated as capital items that residents vote on, and the committee has not yet settled the wording.
watch_next: Position and salary information is to return on a committee agenda in June.
An agenda item to specify the capital planning policy language before a vote is to be sought for the next meeting.
